correctness.rationale: The binary arithmetic recurrence for overlapping `11` pairs generates the four-state substitution. Greedy arches equal universal scattered-subsequence length by direct earliest-embedding and missing-tail-bit arguments. The weighted three-state scanner has explicitly checked k=4 base transformations and algebraic even-to-odd/odd-to-even induction on all 4 letters and all 3 incoming residual states. This proves the dyadic value. Every prefix decomposes into s_2(N) aligned substitution blocks; each block count differs from (5/16) times its length by at most one uniformly in incoming state, proving the exact digit-sum inequality. The standalone verifier independently checks the transform, arithmetic coding, exhaustive defining subsequence property through length 12 and all prefixes up to 131071. Finite replay corroborates; the proof covers all N and k.

value.rationale: The universality index determines the largest scattered-subword length at which a word contains every binary pattern, a central completeness invariant for subsequence problems. Rudin–Shapiro is a classical automatic word with nontrivial substitution structure; the exact rate 5/16 differs from generic binary-word mean rate 1/3, and the all-prefix error bounded by binary Hamming weight is a structural all-scale statement. The even/odd dyadic closed form and uniform bound provide a natural complete quantitative answer, beyond finite tables or an arbitrary slice. It does not rely on an unsupported downstream theorem.
